bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42502963 (freeradius-server): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzzer_dns [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42502963
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: In the staged vulnerable FreeRADIUS checkout `3bb7cd828f502473dc533572a4b3ef33694a9568`, the exact 64-byte witness `20 20 20 20 00 00 20 20 20 20 20 20 01 2d 00 00 0c 20 20 20 20 20 20 00 25 20 20 20 20 20 ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff 20 20 c0 0d` gives `fr_dns_decode()` `QDCOUNT == 0` and `ANCOUNT == 0x2020`, so `decode_record()` enters answer-RR parsing at offset 12. The first RR begins with the name `01 2d 00`; its successful decode both records label block `12..15` in `packet_ctx->lb` and consumes bytes `12..61`, leaving the second RR name as the trailing `c0 0d` at offsets `62..63`. For that second RR, `decode_dns_labels()` first calls `fr_dns_label_uncompressed_length(packet, buf = packet + 62, buf_len = 64, &next, lb)`. The compression pointer resolves to offset `13`, which passes `dns_pointer_valid()` because it lies inside the saved first-name block. After the helper jumps to `packet + 13`, the label-content loop reaches byte `0x00` at offset `14`, and `return -(q - buf)` becomes the positive value `48` because `q = packet + 14` and `buf = packet + 62`. Since that first call returns `48 > 0`, `decode_dns_labels()` skips `goto raw` and keeps `labels_len = next - data = 2`. `fr_dns_label_to_value_box()` immediately repeats the same length probe with `len == 2`; it reaches the same invalid byte `0x00`, returns `48` again, and leaves `after = packet + 64`, so the decode loop still runs. The first vulnerable `dns_label_decode()` call then treats byte `0x2d` at offset `13` as a 45-byte label length and returns `next = packet + 59`. The loop resumes inside prior RR data at bytes `59..60 == ff 20`; a second `dns_label_decode()` interprets those two bytes as compression offset `0x3f20`, assigns `p = packet + 0x3f20` without validating that target, and dereferences `*p` in `*next = p + *p + 1`, producing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ at `src/lib/util/dns.c:1166`. The patch resolves this crash path by passing packet/end into `dns_label_decode()`, rejecting invalid pointer targets before dereference, and propagating negative `slen` returns in `fr_dns_label_to_value_box()`.

source.description: First project-side handoff of the exact malformed second RR slice into structured RR decoding. On iteration 1 this call presents `p = packet + 62`, `end - p = 2`, and trailing bytes `c0 0d`, while `packet_ctx` still carries the full packet and the label blocks accumulated from earlier RR names.
source.value_from: RR iteration 0 returned `slen == 50`, which advanced `p` from `packet + 12` to `packet + 62` and left `packet_ctx->lb` containing the first RR name block `12..15`. The staged witness ends with `c0 0d`, so this call is where that two-byte compressed name becomes the current RR input.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.code: slen = fr_dns_label_to_value_box(vp, &vp->data, data, labels_len, data + total, true, packet_ctx->lb);
tainted_value_origin.description: This call turns the second RR name into the exact helper input that later reaches the sink: after the first positive length-probe return, `decode_dns_labels()` has `labels_len = 2`, so it passes `src = packet + 62`, `label = data + total = packet + 62`, and the accumulated `lb` state into `fr_dns_label_to_value_box()`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. On the second decode pass, only reachable because both prior length probes returned positive `48`, `dns_label_decode()` treats bytes `ff 20` as a compressed-label pointer, computes attacker-controlled offset `0x3f20`, and assigns `p = buf + offset` without checking that the target is backward and within the current packet extent. The patch adds packet/end arguments and rejects exactly these invalid targets before `*p` is used.
root_cause.note: This location is the unfixed hunk in `patch.diff`: the vulnerable helper has no equivalent of the patch's `q >= p`, `*p >= 0xc0`, or `(p + *p + 1) > end` checks, and the caller at `fr_dns_label_to_value_box()` now returns immediately on negative `slen`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After step 11 sets `p` to `packet + 0x3f20`, this statement dereferences `*p` at that wild address to compute the next label pointer.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `dns_label_decode` at `src/lib/util/dns.c:1166:14`, with stack `dns_label_decode -> fr_dns_label_to_value_box -> decode_dns_labels`.

parser_admitted.code: slen = decode_record(ctx, cursor, attr_dns_rr, p, end - p, packet_ctx, packet + 6);
parser_admitted.description: The exact 64-byte witness passes the fixed-header decode and enters the answer-record parser with `p = packet + 12`, `end - p = 52`, and `counter = packet + 6`; that parser path is the only one that reaches the malformed second RR name.

evidence_limitations: Runtime disambiguation is disabled in `run_flags.json`, so the chain is grounded only in the staged vulnerable source, `patch.diff`, the saved AddressSanitizer traces, `reproduction_report.json`, and the exact staged `poc` bytes. Those artifacts are sufficient here because both the pointer-manipulation logic and the crashing dereference are visible in source.

Stage 02 did not execute a fixed build. `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` below is source-grounded from the patch text matching the vulnerable helper and caller, not from dynamic differential validation.

fine_trace.code:
count = fr_net_to_uint16(counter);
for (i = 0; i < count; i++) {
fine_trace.note: For the answer-record decoder, `counter = packet + 6`, so bytes `[6,7] == 0x20 0x20` become `count == 0x2020` (`8224`). That makes the loop attempt at least two RR decodes, which is necessary to reach the trailing `c0 0d` name at offsets `62..63`.

On RR iteration 0, `fr_struct_from_network()` accepts the first RR beginning at offset 12 and returns `slen == 50`: name `01 2d 00` (3 bytes), RR header `00 0c ... 00 25` (10 bytes), and `RDLENGTH == 0x0025` bytes of RDATA (37 bytes). Advancing `p` by 50 moves iteration 1 to offset 62. During that same first RR name decode, `packet_ctx->lb` records block `12..15`, so later pointer offset 13 is treated as landing inside a known DNS-label block.

fine_trace.code:
slen = fr_struct_from_network(ctx, cursor, attr, p, end - p, true,
			      packet_ctx, decode_value_trampoline, NULL);
fine_trace.note: Source. On RR iteration 1, `p = packet + 62`, `end - p = 2`, and the remaining two bytes are exactly `c0 0d`. This call is the first project-side handoff of that malformed RR slice, along with the full-packet context and the prior label blocks, into the RR decoder.

Called from `decode_dns_labels()` with `packet = packet_ctx->packet`, `buf = data = packet + 62`, and `buf_len = data + data_len - packet_ctx->packet = 64`, this helper interprets `c0 0d` as pointer offset `13`. `dns_pointer_valid(lb, 13)` succeeds because step 2 left block `12..15`, `q = packet + 13` points to byte `0x2d` (nonzero and `< 64`), and the first jump therefore sets `*next = packet + 64`.

After step 4 jumps to offset 13, the helper's label-character loop reaches byte `0x00` at offset 14 and executes `return -(q - buf)` at `dns.c:1089`. Because `q = packet + 14` and `buf = packet + 62`, that return value is the positive `48`, not an error. `decode_dns_labels()` therefore sees `slen > 0`, skips `goto raw`, and keeps `labels_len = next - data = 2`.

fine_trace.code: slen = fr_dns_label_to_value_box(vp, &vp->data, data, labels_len, data + total, true, packet_ctx->lb);
fine_trace.note: Tainted value origin. With `labels_len == 2` from step 5, this call hands `fr_dns_label_to_value_box()` the exact crashing RR-name slice: `src = data = packet + 62`, `label = data + total = packet + 62`, and the accumulated `packet_ctx->lb` state.

Called again from `fr_dns_label_to_value_box()` with `buf = src = packet + 62` and `buf_len = len = 2`, the same `c0 0d` pointer again resolves to offset `13`. As in step 4, `dns_pointer_valid(lb, 13)` succeeds and the first jump updates the caller's `after` pointer to `packet + 64`.

This second length probe reaches the same invalid byte `0x00` at offset 14 and returns `48` again via `return -(q - buf)`. Because `slen <= 0` is false at line 1207, `fr_dns_label_to_value_box()` does not return and keeps `after = packet + 64`; that is the second load-bearing positive return needed for the later `dns_label_decode()` calls.

The first `dns_label_decode()` call sees the two RR-name bytes `c0 0d`, computes `offset == 13`, sets `p = packet + 13`, and immediately trusts `*p == 0x2d` as a label length. It returns `slen == 45` and `next == packet + 59`, so the `'-'` byte inside the first RR name is reinterpreted as a 45-byte label header.

With step 9's by-reference updates, `current` was first redirected to offset 13 and `next` to offset 59. This copy reads bytes `14..58`, then advances the loop state to `current = packet + 59`. Because step 8 left `after = packet + 64` and byte 59 is `0xff`, the loop condition remains true for one more `dns_label_decode()` call.

Root cause. The second `dns_label_decode()` call starts at bytes `59..60 == ff 20`, so it computes `offset == 0x3f20` and sets `p = packet + 0x3f20`. The vulnerable helper performs this pointer-target resolution with no check that the target is backward or within the packet/label extent; the patch adds those validations and returns an error here instead.

Sink. After step 11 makes `p` a wild pointer far beyond the 64-byte packet, this statement dereferences `*p` to compute `*next` and return the label length, matching the saved ASan crash at line 1166.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Source-grounded only: `patch.diff` changes `dns_label_decode()` to accept packet/end, adds pointer-target validation before any `*p` dereference, and makes `fr_dns_label_to_value_box()` return immediately on negative `slen`. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

format.name: 64-byte DNS RR pointer witness
format.contract: The staged evidence proves the exact 64-byte witness `20 20 20 20 00 00 20 20 20 20 20 20 01 2d 00 00 0c 20 20 20 20 20 20 00 25 20 20 20 20 20 ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 ff 20 20 c0 0d`. In that exact layout, bytes `[6,7] == 0x20 0x20` make `decode_record()` parse answer RRs; the first RR occupies offsets `12..61` and records label block `12..15`; the trailing `c0 0d` pointer then makes both `fr_dns_label_uncompressed_length()` calls jump to offset `13`, reach invalid byte `0x00` at offset `14`, and return positive `48`; that keeps `labels_len == 2` and `after == packet + 64`, so `dns_label_decode()` later reaches bytes `59..60 == ff 20` and turns them into the wild offset `0x3f20`. The staged artifacts do not prove a broader input class.
